purpose: Recovered, normalized historical investigation patterns for the read-only Code Scout. Historical material informs analysis but never grants mutation authority.

patterns: fail-closed investigation before and during recovery
nine-domain investigation: toolchain, architecture, localization, seo, security, artifact, runtime, browser, build
missing or skipped checks are failures
exact SHA, tree SHA, contract hash, environment fingerprint and normalized failure signatures
shared evidence ledger instead of a parallel evidence system
unknown root cause is a failure, not a pass
deterministic suite registry
explicit command ownership and timeouts
stable contract hashing
normalized failure output for stable signatures
architecture and localization contract coverage
read project governance before code
trigger to propagation path to violated invariant to responsible source to observable symptom
root architectural weakness detection
contract drift detection
single source of truth discovery
invariant extraction
dependency and contract graph analysis
future-error prediction from recurring causes
evidence reproducibility
repair classes instead of one-off symptom fixes
exact SHA binding for analysis snapshots
repository-wide text manifest
explicit exclusions for generated, dependency and secret-like material
analysis bundle can be reproduced from the same commit
recover proven capabilities rather than copying obsolete implementations
preserve QuickFlow, capability registry, pipeline verification, self-correction and memory concepts when compatible
avoid duplicate protocols when an existing contract can absorb the requirement
investigation/audit targets linked to persisted evidence IDs
analysis findings should be traceable to durable evidence
repository-backed technical debt scanning
finding ledger rather than hardcoded reports
surgical remediation rather than broad deletion
